beats.text: Gradient descent finds a curve's lowest point.
Stand on this hill at x equals three.
The rule: step against the slope.
For x squared, slope is two x: six at three, pointing uphill.
So step downhill, scaled by a learning rate of a quarter.
Step one: three minus a quarter of six: one point five.
Step two: zero point seven five.
Step three: zero point three seven five.
X halves each time; height nears zero.
Rate zero point one: x crawls from three to two point four.
Rate one jumps to minus three
